areas.title: Institutional identity and purpose
requirements: Apply the dynamic, participatory, authentic, distinctive identity to every generator surface and deliverable.
Ground claims in real implemented systems, evidence and human purpose; fictional brand examples are not evidence.

areas.title: Naming, voice and written communication
requirements: Use RPI generally and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute formally; retain established proper names without inventing lockups.
Write curious, humble, genuine, resilient, offbeat, relatable copy suited to its audience and medium; avoid unsupported claims and forced slogans.

areas.title: Interface, layout, color and type
requirements: Keep controls and supporting chrome calm while allowing the generated work to be expressive.
Use documented palette and approved compositions; evaluate small UI text contrast independently from logo-color examples.
Use the project RPIGeist/RPIGeistMono system, clear hierarchy, left-aligned multiline text and a measured grid; do not generalize email/video font exceptions to the UI.
Verify keyboard, focus, labels, contrast, reduced motion, scale and pattern interference where affected.

areas.title: Bar systems, logo geometry, motion and exports
requirements: Use official vectors and fixed proportional geometry; retain the 500 by 36 design domain at uniform scale and documented clear space.
Document the encoded or scientific rule, data provenance, assumptions and limitations. Never fabricate measurement.
Preserve preview, header and export parity; never fit painted bounds or rescale individual animation frames to force edge contact.
Review complexity at final placement size; solid-bar minimum sizes do not establish a universal complex-pattern minimum.
Treat gradients/complex-artwork conflicts as unresolved approval questions; do not expand them by assuming existing app behavior is approved.

areas.title: Photography, video and contextual brand applications
requirements: Use authentic people, work and process; protect legibility on imagery and retain appropriate licensing.
Use production-video resolution, audio, caption and template rules only for the production contexts they describe; never stretch a logo to fit an aspect ratio.
Do not use seal, athletics or mascot permissions as generic generator-artwork permissions.
Email fallback fonts are email-specific; gallery examples are inspiration, not blanket permission or technical specifications.

areas.title: Assets, licensing and institutional approvals
requirements: Read actual asset permission records before adding or changing assets; access to the library is not a redistribution license.
Keep Student Union internal-use approval separate from formal official-library approval.
Obtain the applicable written seal/athletics/mascot approvals before new use; do not infer them from this archive.

areas.title: Source and instruction maintenance
requirements: Keep official source captures separate from project interpretation and historical references.
Verify coverage, hashes and source dates; record exclusions, source conflicts and review limits.
Update the source manifest and review fingerprint intentionally. Do not weaken checks or remove a requirement to get a change through.
